newsitem.title: UK: Eastern calls for more power competition.
newsitem.headline: Eastern calls for more power competition.

text.p: Eastern Group, Britain's biggest electricity distributor which has grown into one of the country's largest power generators, called for more competition in the industry on Tuesday.

Jim Whelan, director of gas and energy management at Eastern Group, now part of former Hanson Plc subsidiary Energy Group Plc, told a conference in Stratford that the British power market was still too stifled.
"It (competition) has not gone far enough," he told the three-day conference, adding that this might be rectified as new power plants came on stream.
By 2001 or 2002 "a fairly active generating market will be visible in the UK," he said.

The country's two biggest non-nuclear electricity generators, National Power and PowerGen have been forced to sell off a substantial part of their power plants after accusations that they had too much muscle in the wholesale electricity market.

Despite a host of independent power stations coming on stream and eating into the two companies' domestic margins as competition takes hold, an all-party parliamentary select committee also suggested last week that the two dominant companies sell off more power stations.

Eastern Group, meanwhile, has managed to quietly turn itself into the country's fourth biggest generator after nuclear power group British Energy, by snapping up the power stations that both generators have had to sell off so far.

However, when both generators attempted to branch out into electricity distribution by buying electricity suppliers, they were blocked by the government, which argued that this might be against public interest.
